verdict: IQVIA grew revenue 8% to $4.43B and won $3.2B of new clinical-trial work — its strongest bookings quarter since 2022 — while GAAP net income came to $350M.

segments.name: Research & Development Solutions
segments.note: Running clinical trials for drug makers — net new bookings of $3.2B, up 15%, and a backlog of $32.6B.

segments.name: Commercial Solutions
segments.note: Data, analytics and technology that help drug makers sell and market their products.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling and running a 90,000-person global services business.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of past acquisitions and equipment over time.

opex.name: Restructuring costs
opex.note: Reshaping the business under its new, simpler two-segment structure.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $203M, partly offset by $42M of earnings from unconsolidated affiliates, $12M of interest income and $5M of other income — a net $144M cost.

takeaways.title: Bookings are surging
takeaways.text: R&D Solutions won $3.2B of net new business, up 15% — a 1.2x book-to-bill — and last-twelve-month bookings reached $11.7B.

takeaways.title: Cash conversion is strong
takeaways.text: Free cash flow of $667M was 120% of adjusted net income; net debt stood at $13.8B, or 3.45x adjusted EBITDA.

takeaways.title: Guidance raised
takeaways.text: IQVIA lifted its full-year outlook: revenue of $17.35–17.50B and adjusted EPS of $12.90–$13.00.

footerNote: Net income of $352M is before $2M attributable to noncontrolling interests; net income attributable to IQVIA was $350M, the basis for the $2.10 EPS. A review of inactive trials also removed about $2.1B from reported backlog — an accounting cleanup with no effect on revenue or profit.
